key_insight: The paper proposes a single modality-invariant Neural Health Index (NHI) that summarizes resting-brain energy organization into one score to separate healthy from clinical populations.
clinical_relevance: If validated broadly, NHI could help with disease stratification and treatment monitoring across neurological, psychiatric, neurodevelopmental, and neurodegenerative conditions.
method: Derived an energetic profile from resting EEG, MEG, or fMRI signal energy distributions.
Combined five features: lognormality, balanced spatial allocation, inter-regional independence, low variance, and temporal stability.
Compressed the profile into a single NHI score for cross-modality comparison.
evidence_signal: In 808 participants, NHI reportedly distinguished healthy from clinical groups with >95% sensitivity and specificity in internal and external validation and generalized across unseen diagnoses.
watch_item: The abstract reports strong validation, but real-world deployment will depend on independent replication, harmonized acquisition pipelines, and testing across sites and modalities.
paper_title: A Modality-Invariant Measure of Neural Health
